title: Discrete-Time Signal Processing, MIT 6.341, Fall 2005
where: MIT OpenCourseWare's official course site provides the complete published course corpus at https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-341-discrete-time-signal-processing-fall-2005/. shards.note: Course overview and foundations through phase, minimum-phase/all-pass systems, continuous/discrete-time conversion, sampling-rate conversion, quantization/noise shaping, filter structures, and IIR filter design; include the background exam and its solution. Seven lecture-note PDFs are posted in this range.

FIR design, multirate/polyphase structures, linear prediction, Levinson-Durbin recursion, the DFT, and DFT-based linear filtering; include the midterm and its solution. Seven lecture-note PDFs are posted in this range.

DFT spectral analysis, periodograms, FFT algorithms, Goertzel and chirp transforms, short-time Fourier analysis, and modulated filter banks; include both projects, supporting data/code, and the final exam with its solution. Six lecture-note PDFs are posted in this range.

notes: The official MIT OCW pages identify Prof. Alan V. Oppenheim as instructor and the offering as graduate course 6.341, Fall 2005. The lecture schedule contains 23 meetings; downloadable notes are posted for Lectures 2–13 and 15–22 (20 readable PDFs), while Lectures 1, 14, and 23 are listed without note PDFs. The assignments page provides a homework contract plus Problem Sets 1–11 and a separate solution PDF for every set. The exams page provides Fall 2005 and Fall 2004 background, midterm, and final exams, each with a solution. The projects page provides one instructions PDF covering two projects, two MAT files for Project 1, a ZIP of 52 WAV files for Project 2, and two MATLAB audio helpers. The readings page enumerates the required second-edition textbook, one optional MATLAB exercise book, nine articles/papers of interest, and five recommended books; those third-party readings are bibliographic references and are not bundled with the open course package. Access is classified as full for the complete MIT-published course corpus, not for the separately published required textbook.
